messages:
jen: Heads-up — planning to roll v14 of the client libraries next week. Release notes flag three user-impacting changes: (1) auth parameter renamed from \`apiKey\` -> \`auth_token\`, (2) default retry strategy changed from exponential to adaptive which can increase 429s surfaced to callers, (3) streaming chunk framing now yields \`data: [partial]\` events instead of raw token blocks. Want a quick checklist before we open the announcement/PRs.

sam: Thanks for the callout. Do we have a short migration guide for each language? Node/Python/Go folks always hit different footguns.

jen: Not yet, that's what I wanted to gather. Quick notes I have:
- Node: auth rename is breaking for consumers who pass { apiKey } to the constructor. Suggest we add a deprecation cycle: v13 accept both with warning, v14 require \`auth_token\`.
- Python: streaming change affects async iterators; users who relied on raw token chunking will need to switch to the new \`stream.on_data\` handler.
- Go: retry strategy default changes might surface more errors in customers with short timeouts; recommend documenting how to set \`DisableAdaptiveRetry=true\`.

elaine: Can we do the deprecation header thing? i.e., warn on startup if \`apiKey\` used and link to migration doc.

sam: +1 for runtime warning. Also propose adding a compatibility helper function in each SDK: \`compat_from_old_config(old_cfg)\` to reduce churn.

liam: For streaming, can we include a tiny code snippet for Node and Python in the migration doc? e.g., Node:
```\n// v13 style (raw tokens)\nclient.stream((chunk)=>console.log(chunk))\n\n// v14 style\nclient.stream.on('data', (evt)=>{\n  if(evt.type==='partial') handlePartial(evt.payload)\n})\n```
And Python example using async for vs callback.

jen: Perfect. Also, we should be explicit about semantic of adaptive retries: it increases inter-request batching which reduces requests but can cause bursts counted as 429s until the backoff warms up. Ops has seen this before.

elaine: Ops ask: is there a recommended default to keep current behavior? If yes we should add it to the changelog and the quick migration snippet.

sam: There is: passing \`retry={'strategy':'exponential'}\` preserves previous behavior. We'll document the flag in all SDKs. We should also expose a top-level API: \`client.configure({compat: true})\` to toggle all compatibility options.

jen: Can someone own the public-facing migration doc + in-repo deprecation warnings? I'll open the release branch once items merged.

liam: I can draft the Node and JS snippets + PR for runtime warnings.

elaine: I'll do Python + CI test that validates streaming behavior changes (integration test that asserts event framing).

sam: I'll cover Go and the compatibility helpers. Also will add the changelog snippet for the retry toggle.

jen: Great — timeline: PRs by EOD Thu, merge Fri morning, docs + announcement Fri afternoon. Anyone need extra time?

liam: EOD Thu works for me but may need basic review help.

elaine: Same.

sam: Allocated time to review. I'll queue SRE for a quick load test preview on the staging cluster after merge.

upgrade-bot: Automatic notice: Deprecation policy: will warn for 2 minor releases before enforcement. Telemetry event created: \"clientlib.v14.migration.start\".

jen: Thanks all — I'll create the release checklist and link PRs here when created. Also adding a short code-mod script suggestion for repo maintainers to rename \`apiKey\` -> \`auth_token\` in sample apps.

sam: Nice. One more thought — update the SDK quickstarts on the website on the same day of release to avoid confusion.

jen: Agreed. Posting a final task list: (1) runtime warnings PR (Node/Python/Go) — liam/elaine/sam; (2) migration doc + snippets — liam/elaine; (3) changelog + rollback knobs — sam; (4) release announcement draft — jen. I'll ping again once PRs are up. :thumbsup:
